body: Would be great to move this `stdout` parsing logic in to another function, where we could write a test or two against it?
Should we limit the maximum depth here to some small reasonable number? Though I realise this will potentially compromise accuracy..

For the first iteration: we could consider use the cached data from `context.get_dir_files()` and `find()` rather than hitting the OS again.

This code is simpler though, so it's probably worth measuring...

I'm personally not a huge fan of the long error in the prompt. Can we throw in some config to toggle this? Perhaps we could hide the whole module if this fails, or perhaps a single "alert" symbol to indicate something is wrong but without saying what.
Right. I moved the part to `extract_toolchain_from_rustup_override_list` and added a test for it.
Now it displays toolchain name (`channel-triple`). I updated the screenshot.

I don't think this degrades the performance so much. Its behavior is same as [`~/.cargo/bin/rustc --version`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup.rs/blob/d84e6e50126bccd84649e42482fc35a11d019401/src/config.rs#L320-L358
).
My benchmarks suggests this is about 30% slower. That said, I think it is quick enough - under 100ms on most systems and under 50ms on systems with fast I/O.
